title: How India’s Day Traders Broke the World’s Biggest Options Market
description_html:
When millions of retail investors piled into India’s options market to get rich quick, losses mounted and regulators launched a sweeping crackdown. 

On today’s Big Take Asia podcast, guest host Rebecca Choong Wilkins and India equities reporter Savio Shetty break down how the world’s largest options market unraveled, why regulators are struggling to police the country’s latest craze and where traders are placing their bets now. 

Read more: How India Built (and Broke) the World’s Biggest Options Casino

Further listening: Inside Jane Street: The Enigmatic Firm That Rules Wall Street

Watch, from Originals: How India's Day Retail Traders Lost Billions

Host: Rebecca Choong Wilkins; Guest: Savio Shetty; Produced by Naomi Ng and Yang Yang; Edited by Crispina Robert and Julia Weaver. Engineering by Sean Carter II.

It's not easy.

Which I think is highly unlikely.
Given that commodities are far more volatile than equities.

There is nothing called get rich quick.
I think for regulators, it is probably very easy to blame and say, you know, You should have looked at these products before.
How can you do this?
How can you do that?
But India was accused of being closed for a very long time for not having this.
So you have to balance that.

There were a lot of things that probably went wrong.

Absolutely has. I have no doubt that it has.
But I think with the way things move in financial markets, there is always something new that someone will manufacture.
Maybe the regulators loosen regulations a bit.
Here and there.
And you will always have that.

The aftermath will be that derivatives, as Warren Buffett had once called them, are weapons of mass destruction.
If you do not know what they are, it will blast and it will leave a crater.
And as with most craters, they don't get filled with over time.
They might become a bit less visible, but they still exist.

I'm Rebecca Chung Wilkins.

Thanks for listening.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Savio, what is the lesson here?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I think it depends on who you ask what the lesson is. If you ask the person who burnt his entire savings, it would be probably not jump on every fad that comes in. There is nothing called get rich quick. I think for regulators, it is probably very easy to blame and say, you know, You should have looked at these products before. How can you do this? How can you do that?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: But India was accused of being closed for a very long time for not having this.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So you have to balance that.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: But I think the overlying part here is that Indians retail traders lost billions of dollars. We've had people who've taken debts for five years, 10 years, money lenders calling them, uh, weddings of sons and daughters being pushed forward.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Maybe not even happening.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And I think that is something that kind of comes back to me, that beyond just moving numbers on the screen, there were dreams that were crushed.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: There were a lot of things that probably went wrong.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: When you get these big moments, these sort of boom and bust cycles, it does sometimes leave a scar on the population and it can make them hesitant to invest again. I'm curious, sort of big picture, do you think this has left any kind of aftermath sort of psychologically on the retail investor?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Absolutely has. I have no doubt that it has. But I think with the way things move in financial markets, there is always something new that someone will manufacture. Maybe the regulators loosen regulations a bit.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Here and there.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And you will always have that. So I don't think the boom and bust cycle will ever, ever, you know, stop. The aftermath will be that derivatives, as Warren Buffett had once called them, are weapons of mass destruction. If you do not know what they are, it will blast and it will leave a crater. And as with most craters, they don't get filled with over time. They might become a bit less visible, but they still exist.

study.one_liner_ko: 팬데믹 이후 인도 개인투자자들이 옵션 시장에 몰려 수십억 달러를 잃은 과정과, 규제 당국의 대응 및 투기 자금이 상품시장으로 옮겨간 현상을 다룬 에피소드.
summary_ko: 인도는 거래량 기준 세계 최대 주식옵션 시장이다. 팬데믹 때 개인투자자가 폭발적으로 늘었고 월가의 정교한 트레이딩 회사들도 몰려들었다.
저렴한 데이터 요금(Reliance Jio), 초저가 수수료 중개사, 하루 만에 가능한 계좌 개설, 최소 증거금 없는 거래, 팬데믹 불안이 겹쳐 '퍼펙트 스톰'이 만들어졌다. 개인투자자는 100만 명 미만에서 약 1,000만 명으로 늘었다.
옵션은 레버리지가 매우 커서 방향뿐 아니라 타이밍도 맞혀야 한다. 인도 증권당국(SEBI) 조사에서 개인의 약 90%가 손실을 봤고, 2022~2025년에 330억 달러 넘게 사라졌다. 이익은 주로 고빈도매매(HFT) 업체가 가져갔다.
SEBI는 제인 스트리트가 지수를 조작했다며 일시 영업정지를 내렸고 추정 순이익은 43억 달러였다. 회사는 혐의를 부인하고 항소했다. 당국은 계약 최소 규모를 약 3배로 올리고 주간 만기 지수옵션을 하나로 줄였다. 거래량은 30~40% 감소했다.
투기 열기는 금 등 상품시장과 ETF로 옮겨갔다. 상품시장에는 주간옵션이 없어 같은 광풍이 재현될 가능성은 낮다고 본다. 규제 당국은 시장 육성과 투기 억제 사이에서 균형을 잡기 어렵다.
Savio는 숫자 너머로 빚, 미뤄진 결혼식, 무너진 꿈이 있었다고 말한다. 호황과 불황의 사이클은 계속될 것이고, 파생상품은 버핏의 말처럼 '대량살상무기'로 상처를 남긴다고 본다.
study.summary_en: This episode is about how India became the world's biggest options market and what went wrong. During the pandemic, cheap data, ultra-low brokerage fees and easy account opening pulled millions of retail traders in. Options are highly leveraged, so you have to get both the direction and the timing right. The regulator found that roughly nine in ten retail traders were losing money, and more than thirty-three billion dollars was wiped out, while high-frequency firms like Jane Street came out ahead. SEBI tightened the rules and volumes fell, and the speculative energy has shifted to commodities and ETFs. The takeaway is that regulating this is a delicate balance, and boom-and-bust cycles probably won't stop.

examples: We need a venue for forty people, and this café fits the bill.

examples: Every streaming company wants a piece of the pie in live sports.

expressions.nuance_ko: 좋던 상황이 나빠지거나 유리하던 쪽이 뒤바뀔 때 쓴다. 내레이션이나 스토리텔링에서 반전 포인트를 짚는 장치로 좋다. 'The tide is turning'처럼 진행형도 흔하다.

You could tell the wind had changed in the room.

expressions.quote: people who had no clue what an option was

examples: I had no clue the meeting had been moved to Thursday.
Half the audience had no clue what the acronym meant.
She has no clue how much that flight will cost.

similar.example: I haven't the faintest idea where he went.
He's clueless about cooking.

expressions.quote: Indians have always shied away from the stock markets
expressions.nuance_ko: 부담이나 두려움 때문에 회피하는 태도를 말한다. 'shy away from + 명사/동명사' 구조이고 부정문('doesn't shy away from controversy')으로도 많이 쓴다.

expressions.quote: I think it was the perfect storm
expressions.meaning_ko: 여러 악재(또는 요인)가 동시에 겹친 최악의 상황
expressions.nuance_ko: 원래 나쁜 요인이 겹칠 때 쓰지만 여기서는 요인들이 겹쳐 열풍이 만들어졌다는 뜻이다. 'a perfect storm of A, B and C' 형태로 요인을 나열하면 논리가 선명해진다.
examples: Rising rents and a hiring freeze created a perfect storm for young renters.
The strike, the weather and a software outage made it a perfect storm for the airline.
A perfect storm of cheap credit and low rates inflated the housing market.

similar.example: It was a confluence of factors, not one cause.

expressions.quote: As more ordinary people piled into the market
expressions.nuance_ko: 군중이 한꺼번에 어떤 시장·자산·장소로 몰릴 때 쓴다. 투자 열풍이나 쏠림을 묘사하기 좋다. 'pile in'도 가능하고 약간 무분별하다는 뉘앙스가 있다.
examples: Investors piled into tech stocks last year.

expressions.meaning_ko: 나쁜 것을 없애려다 좋은 것까지 버리다
expressions.nuance_ko: 개혁이나 규제가 과해서 장점까지 없앴다는 비판에 쓴다. 정책 토론, 회의에서 신중론을 펼 때 유용하다. 'accused of ...ing'와 함께 쓰이는 경우가 많다.
examples: Let's fix the process, not scrap the whole system and throw the baby out with the bathwater.
Cutting every cost line risks throwing the baby out with the bathwater.

similar.example: We overcorrected after the first complaint.

expressions.quote: going back to the heydays of India's derivatives boom
expressions.nuance_ko: 과거의 가장 좋았던 시절을 가리키며 'in its heyday' 형태로 자주 쓴다. 단수 'heyday'가 표준이고 방송에서는 복수 'heydays'도 들린다. 다시 오지 않을 시절이라는 뉘앙스가 있다.

similar.example: This was the golden age of the music industry.

expressions.quote: we sometimes don't give regulators enough credit
expressions.nuance_ko: 'give X credit for Y'는 공이나 어려움을 인정해줄 때 쓴다. 'don't give enough credit'은 과소평가한다는 방어 논리에서 자주 나온다. 상대 입장을 옹호하며 균형을 잡는 데 유용하다.

expressions.quote: eager to cash in on a rapidly growing market
